findings.title: website_name is not in untrusted_attributes, leaking hidden website data of TL0 users to anonymous visitors
findings.body: The serializer hides `website` (and other untrusted attributes) for TL0 users viewed anonymously via `untrusted_attributes :website, ...` (line 109), so that anonymous users cannot see a TL0 user's profile website. However the newly added `website_name` attribute (line 43) is not added to that list, and its `include_website_name` predicate only checks `website.present?`. As a result, for a TL0 user viewed anonymously, the JSON payload will omit `website` but still include `website_name`, which contains the host and full path of that website — effectively bypassing the privacy restriction and leaking exactly the information the untrusted_attributes mechanism is meant to hide. Add `:website_name` to the `untrusted_attributes` list.

findings.title: include_website_name is missing the trailing question mark, so AMS never uses it as an inclusion predicate
findings.body: ActiveModel::Serializers determines inclusion by calling `include_#{attribute}?` (with a question mark). The method here is defined as `include_website_name` (line 153) without the `?`, so it is never invoked by the serializer framework. The consequence is that `website_name` is serialized unconditionally: for users with no website the payload will contain a `website_name: null` key (inconsistent with other optional attributes like `website_name` being expected to be absent), and any future conditional logic placed in this method will silently not run. Rename to `include_website_name?`.

findings.title: website_name drops query string and fragment from the website URL
findings.body: When the website domain matches the instance domain, `website_name` is built as `website_host + URI(website.to_s).path`, which discards the query string and fragment. A user whose website is `https://example.com/page?id=42` would see the profile display `example.com/page`, which is not the complete URL path the PR intends to show and could mislead users about where the link points. Include `URI(...).query` and `fragment` when present.

findings.title: No test that website_name is hidden for TL0 users seen anonymously
findings.body: The existing 'with a TL0 user seen as anonymous' context asserts that all untrusted attributes (including `website`) are not serialized, but the new `website_name` attribute is not added to that assertion list. Combined with the fact that `website_name` was not added to `untrusted_attributes` in the serializer, this test gap allowed a privacy regression to slip through. Add `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` in the spec (and set a website on the fabricated user profile so the leak would be caught).
